sets.title: Vocabulary · everyday words (set 3)
sets.instruction: Choose the word that fits the sentence best.

questions.q: The soup was too hot, so Mei blew on it to make it __________.
Our teacher asked us to __________ in a straight line.
questions.tip: To 'queue' is to stand in a line.

questions.q: The puppy was so __________ that it fitted into one hand.
Ravi __________ the door gently so as not to wake the baby.
questions.tip: 'Closed' is the gentle word; the others are noisy.

questions.q: The bag was so __________ that I had to use both hands.
We could see the bottom of the pool because the water was very __________.
The bread had gone __________ after three days in the tin.
My father's car is __________ than my uncle's van.
Please put the rubbish in the __________.
The kitten was __________ of the vacuum cleaner.
Nadia was __________ when she got a sticker for her work.
The floor was slippery, so we walked __________.
He __________ his shoelaces before the race.
The sun was so bright that I had to __________ my eyes.
questions.tip: To 'shade' your eyes is to shield them.

questions.q: My grandmother __________ me a story every Sunday.
questions.tip: 'Tell' takes a person and a story.

questions.q: We waited at the bus __________ outside our block for ten minutes, but only taxis went past.
questions.tip: A bus picks up passengers at a bus stop; a bus station is where many routes begin.

questions.q: The soup needs more salt because it tastes of __________.
questions.tip: 'Tastes of nothing' means it has no taste at all.

questions.q: Gopal is the __________ boy in our class; he is taller than everyone.
The library is __________ on Sundays, so we went on Monday.
Please __________ the window; the room is stuffy.
questions.tip: A stuffy room needs air, so open the window.

questions.q: The shirt was too small, so my mother __________ it to my cousin.
A __________ of birds flew over the field.
The ice cream began to __________ in the sun.
questions.tip: 'Melt' means to turn from solid to liquid.

questions.q: He wiped the table with a damp __________.
questions.tip: A cloth is used for wiping.

questions.q: The path was very __________, so we had to climb slowly.
Our dog __________ loudly whenever the doorbell rings.
Siti __________ the flour and the eggs together in a bowl.
The baby is __________, so please speak softly.
I __________ my bicycle to school every day.
The floor was __________ with sand after the beach trip.
Please __________ your name at the top of the page.
There were __________ people on the bus, so we all got a seat.
The kite flew high because the wind was __________.
questions.tip: A strong wind lifts a kite.

questions.q: He was __________ after running twice round the field.
Mrs Ong __________ the register every morning.
questions.tip: 'Take the register' is the set phrase.

questions.q: The milk has gone __________; do not drink it.
We washed our __________ before we ate.
The lift was __________, so we took the stairs.
Please be __________; the baby is sleeping.
My sister is __________ at drawing than I am.
The parcel was __________ in brown paper.
There is a __________ in my sock where my toe shows.
The teacher asked us to __________ our books on the shelf.
We __________ the bird fly away from the branch.
The shop sells __________ of every colour.
questions.tip: 'Of every colour' needs a plural noun.

questions.q: It was so cold that we could see our __________.
Please __________ the rubbish out before dinner.
questions.tip: 'Take out the rubbish' is the set phrase.

questions.q: The cat sat __________ the mat and would not move.
My uncle __________ in a hospital as a nurse.
I could not find my pencil case __________.

sets.title: Shades of meaning · choosing the right strength
sets.instruction: All four options are close in meaning. Choose the one whose strength fits the sentence.

questions.q: The water in the kettle was __________ — it was bubbling fiercely.
questions.tip: 'Boiling' is the strongest degree of hot.

questions.q: The afternoon was pleasantly __________, not hot at all.
It was so __________ outside that the tar on the road had softened.
He was __________ about losing the match but got over it by dinner.
questions.tip: 'Disappointed' is mild; 'devastated' would be far stronger.

questions.q: She was __________ when her grandmother's ring was stolen.
questions.tip: The loss is serious, so the strong word fits.

questions.q: I was __________ by the noise from the flat above, though I soon got used to it.
questions.tip: 'Soon got used to it' shows the feeling was mild.

questions.q: The referee was __________ when the player spat at him, and sent him off at once.
questions.tip: Spitting at a person and an instant sending-off point to the strongest word.

questions.q: The soup was __________; we finished it, but nobody asked for more.
questions.tip: 'Tasty' is moderate praise; the other three all claim far more than 'nobody asked for more'.

questions.q: The sound of the drill was __________ and gave me a headache.
From the other room came a __________ hum I could barely hear.
The path was __________ in places, but never so sharp that we had to use our hands.
questions.tip: 'Never so sharp that we needed our hands' rules out the three stronger words.

questions.q: He gave the door a __________ push and it swung open without a sound.
questions.tip: 'Without a sound' shows the push was soft.

questions.q: She was __________ of spiders and would not enter the shed.
questions.tip: Refusing to enter shows extreme fear.

questions.q: I am a little __________ of dogs I do not know.
The old bridge was so __________ that two planks gave way as we crossed.
questions.tip: All four describe a poor bridge, but only 'rickety' carries the sense of falling apart.

questions.q: He is __________ of his sister's exam results and tells everyone how hard she worked.
questions.tip: Telling everyone how hard she worked shows pleasure at her success, not envy.

questions.q: The queue moved __________; we waited almost an hour.
questions.tip: An hour's wait means slow movement.

questions.q: She answered __________, before I had even finished asking.
The room was __________ after the party — nothing was in its place.
questions.tip: 'Chaotic' is the strongest word for disorder.

questions.q: My desk is a little __________ but I know where everything is.
The soup was __________; I had three bowls.
questions.tip: Three bowls means it was very good.

questions.q: The meal was __________ — not good, but we were hungry enough.
questions.tip: 'Edible' means only just good enough to eat.

questions.q: He made a __________ mistake that cost the team the match.
questions.tip: Costing the match makes it serious.

questions.q: There was a __________ difference between the two shades of blue.
questions.tip: Two shades of the same colour differ only slightly.

questions.q: The crowd was __________ when the goal was disallowed, but nobody left their seat.
questions.tip: 'Nobody left their seat' shows the anger stopped short of the three stronger words.

questions.q: She looked __________ when I explained it a second time.
questions.tip: Needing a second explanation suggests confusion.

questions.q: After the hike we were __________ and fell asleep in the car.
questions.tip: Falling asleep at once means more than tired.

questions.q: I am a bit __________ this evening but I can finish the chapter.
The rain was __________; we were soaked in ten seconds.
A __________ drizzle was falling, hardly enough to wet the path.
questions.tip: 'Light' matches 'hardly enough to wet the path'.

questions.q: He gave a __________ answer and would say nothing more.
Her explanation was __________ and covered every step.
The shop was __________; one customer stood at the counter and nobody else.
questions.tip: One customer means it was not deserted or empty — only quiet.

questions.q: The train was __________; we had to stand but there was room to turn round.
questions.tip: 'Room to turn round' rules out the three stronger words.

questions.q: He was __________ about the trip and could talk of nothing else.
I am __________ to help if you need me.
The old photograph had __________ a little, though the faces were still clear.
questions.tip: 'Still clear' shows only slight loss of colour.

questions.q: The glass __________ into hundreds of pieces on the tiles.
There is a small __________ in the cup but it still holds tea.
questions.tip: A 'chip' is a tiny piece broken off.

questions.q: Her voice was __________ with excitement, though she was trying hard to sound calm.
questions.tip: 'Trying hard to sound calm' shows she was not succeeding.

sets.title: Connectors for writing · 30 items
sets.instruction: Choose the connector that shows the right relationship between the two ideas.

questions.q: The bus broke down. __________ (Consequently / Meanwhile / Similarly), we arrived an hour late.
The rain had stopped. __________ (Nevertheless / Therefore / Likewise), the pitch was still unplayable.
questions.tip: 'Nevertheless' shows a contrast with what you would expect.

questions.q: Wei Jie prepared the slides. __________ (Meanwhile / However / Consequently), Priya practised the speech.
questions.tip: 'Meanwhile' shows two things happening at the same time.

questions.q: Cycling is cheap. __________ (Moreover / However / Nevertheless), it keeps you fit.
questions.tip: 'Moreover' adds a further point in the same direction.

questions.q: The recipe looked simple. __________ (In fact / Therefore / Similarly), it took three hours.
questions.tip: 'In fact' corrects the impression just given.

questions.q: She trained every morning. __________ (As a result / However / Meanwhile), she broke her own record.
Dogs need daily walks. __________ (Similarly / However / Instead), rabbits need daily handling.
He did not enjoy the film. __________ (Nonetheless / Therefore / Likewise), he stayed until the end.
We could take the train. __________ (Alternatively / Consequently / Furthermore), we could walk.
We had planned to work in the library, but it was shut. __________ (Instead / Moreover / Therefore), we worked in the canteen.
questions.tip: 'Instead' introduces what was done in place of the original plan.

questions.q: Plastic bottles take centuries to break down. __________ (Furthermore / However / Meanwhile), most are never recycled.
questions.tip: 'Furthermore' adds another point on the same side.

questions.q: The plan was expensive. __________ (On the other hand / As a result / Likewise), it would last twenty years.
questions.tip: 'On the other hand' introduces the opposing consideration.

questions.q: First we washed the tins. __________ (Next / However / Therefore), we flattened them.
We have settled the costs and the timetable. __________ (Finally / Firstly / Meanwhile), I would like to thank the volunteers.
questions.tip: Two points have already been made, so this is the last one.

questions.q: The road will be resurfaced from June until August. __________ (In the meantime / Consequently / Similarly), buses will use Jalan Bahru.
questions.tip: 'In the meantime' means during that period.

questions.q: He is the youngest in the team. __________ (Even so / Therefore / Likewise), he is the captain.
__________ (Although / Despite / However) it was raining, the match went ahead.
questions.tip: 'Although' introduces a clause; 'despite' needs a noun.

questions.q: __________ (Despite / Although / However) the rain, the match went ahead.
questions.tip: 'Despite' is followed by a noun, not a clause.

questions.q: The shop sells bread and cakes __________ (but / and / or) no longer bakes biscuits.
questions.tip: The second idea contradicts what you would expect from the first.

questions.q: __________ (Whereas / Because / Therefore) my brother likes durian, I cannot stand it.
The experiment failed twice. __________ (Eventually / Immediately / Similarly), it worked.
Read the whole question. __________ (Only then / Meanwhile / Likewise) should you begin to write.
She is a careful driver. __________ (By contrast / Similarly / Furthermore), her brother is reckless.
questions.tip: 'By contrast' sets one against the other.

questions.q: I have three things to tell you. __________ (To begin with / Finally / Meanwhile), let me explain why the trip was cancelled.
questions.tip: Three points are promised, so this is the first of them.

questions.q: The cost is high. __________ (That said / Therefore / Likewise), the results speak for themselves.
questions.tip: 'That said' concedes a point before disagreeing.

questions.q: He apologised. __________ (Even then / Therefore / Similarly), she would not speak to him.
questions.tip: 'Even then' means despite that having happened.

questions.q: Wear closed shoes. __________ (Otherwise / Therefore / Meanwhile), you will not be allowed in.
questions.tip: 'Otherwise' states what happens if the advice is ignored.

questions.q: __________ (In conclusion / For instance / Meanwhile), the scheme should be continued for another term.
Many everyday objects contain magnets — __________ (for instance / therefore / however), fridge doors and headphones.
The bin was full. __________ (Rather than / Therefore / Similarly) leave the cup on top, he carried it downstairs.
questions.tip: 'Rather than' contrasts what was done with what was not.
